description: Diagnostic decision tree mapping audio symptoms to EQ solutions
usage: Use this to build smart assistants, troubleshooting guides, or learning tools that recommend specific band archetypes based on user-described problems

priorityLevels.1: Critical - Fix first, these cause major mix problems
priorityLevels.2: Important - Address after critical issues are resolved
priorityLevels.3: Polish - Final touches for professional sound

rules.description: Mix feels bloated, limiter pumps, or sounds like there's inaudible low-end taking up space

recommendations.notes: Use HP 70-100 Hz on all non-bass sources. This is the #1 fix for headroom issues.
recommendations.context: Apply to: vocals, guitars, keys, synths, percussion (not kick/bass)

rules.description: Mix sounds like there's a blanket over the speakers, lacks definition, congested low-mids

recommendations.notes: Small cuts in 200-300 Hz clear mixes extremely quickly. Start with -2 dB.
recommendations.context: Apply to: multiple tracks with low-mid buildup, mix bus if widespread

recommendations.notes: If 250 Hz cut is too aggressive, try wider cut at 200 Hz
recommendations.context: Alternative if you want to preserve some warmth

rules.description: Mix hurts to listen to, causes ear fatigue, sounds sharp or aggressive

recommendations.notes: Cut 4-6 kHz; use narrow BW only for obvious resonances. Start gentle.
recommendations.context: Common in vocals, guitars, cymbals - sweep to find exact frequency

recommendations.notes: If harshness is in presence range (2-3 kHz), cut here instead
recommendations.context: Alternative if the harshness is more 'edgy' than 'sharp'

rules.description: Sounds like it was recorded in a small room, enclosed, cardboard-like quality

recommendations.notes: Use medium BW; avoid over-cutting or you'll lose life. Sweep 300-550 Hz to find it.
recommendations.context: Common in: vocals, acoustic guitars, drums, poorly recorded sources

recommendations.notes: If boxiness is lower in frequency range
recommendations.context: Try 350 Hz if 420 Hz doesn't hit the right spot

rules.description: Vocals or instruments sound pinched, nasal, honky, or have a cheap tone

recommendations.notes: Small changes only - this range is very sensitive. Sweep 700-1000 Hz.
recommendations.context: Common in: vocals, guitars, brass, anything with midrange focus

recommendations.notes: Try lower frequency for male vocals or lower-pitched sources
recommendations.context: Alternative for male vocals or deeper instruments

recommendations.notes: Try higher frequency for female vocals or higher-pitched sources
recommendations.context: Alternative for female vocals or brighter instruments

rules.description: Vocals or lead elements disappear in the mix, lack intelligibility, can't hear lyrics clearly

recommendations.notes: Presence makes vocals and leads intelligible. Don't overdo it - can cause harshness.
recommendations.context: Apply to: lead vocals, lead synths, main melodic elements

recommendations.notes: Try lower frequency for male vocals
recommendations.context: Better for deeper male voices

recommendations.notes: Try higher frequency for female vocals
recommendations.context: Better for female voices or brighter sources

rules.description: Source sounds thin, weak, lacks weight or physical presence

recommendations.notes: Add gentle warmth and thickness. Don't overdo - this range stacks fast.
recommendations.context: Apply to: thin vocals, weak guitars, sources needing fullness

recommendations.notes: Specifically for adding chest resonance to vocals
recommendations.context: Great for male vocals or adding depth/power

recommendations.notes: Rare boost in boxiness range for very thin sources
recommendations.context: Only if source is extremely thin and needs midrange weight

rules.description: Mix sounds dark, dull, closed, lacks excitement or sparkle

recommendations.notes: Use a wide high shelf for polish. Keep it subtle on buses/master.
recommendations.context: Final polish - apply to tracks, buses, or master for modern sheen

recommendations.notes: Lower shelf for more body to the air boost
recommendations.context: If 12k sounds too airy without enough presence

recommendations.notes: If dullness is more about lack of detail than air
recommendations.context: Add definition and crispness before adding air

rules.description: Source sounds soft, lacks snap, consonants are weak, transients are dull

recommendations.notes: Small boosts add definition. Watch for sibilance and harshness.
recommendations.context: Apply to: vocals, percussion, anything needing articulation

recommendations.notes: Higher frequency for more snap and attack
recommendations.context: Better for percussion, drums, sharp transients

rules.description: Harsh S sounds, overly bright cymbals, too much high-frequency energy

recommendations.notes: Cut upper harshness and sibilance. Use medium-narrow BW.
recommendations.context: Common issue with vocals - sweep 5-7 kHz to find exact frequency

recommendations.notes: If entire top-end is too bright, not just one frequency
recommendations.context: Use high shelf cut for overly bright sources

rules.description: Recording has noise, hiss, or unwanted high-frequency artifacts

recommendations.notes: High shelf cut to reduce noise and artifacts. Keep it wide.
recommendations.context: For noisy recordings - but use noise reduction first if available

rules.description: Excessive sub-bass, boomy low-end, sound feels out of control in the lows

recommendations.notes: More aggressive HP to tighten low-end. Adjust frequency to taste.
recommendations.context: For overly boomy sources or modern tight sound

rules.description: Overall tone sounds unprofessional, cheap, or amateurish

recommendations.notes: Boxiness is often what makes things sound cheap. Remove cardboard tone.
recommendations.context: First step in making things sound 'expensive'

recommendations.notes: Air adds professional polish and modern sheen
recommendations.context: Second step - add gloss and finish

rules.description: Source doesn't hit hard, lacks punch or physical impact

recommendations.notes: Boost fundamental frequency for more weight (kick/bass only)
recommendations.context: Only for kick/bass - sweep 40-60 Hz to find fundamental

recommendations.notes: Presence can add perceived punch and attack
recommendations.context: For non-bass elements - adds attack perception

rules.description: Source sounds like it's in the back of the mix, far from the listener

recommendations.notes: Presence brings sounds forward and closer to listener
recommendations.context: Primary tool for bringing sources forward

recommendations.notes: Warmth can also add proximity/closeness
recommendations.context: Adds intimacy and 'close-mic' feel

rules.description: Sound is too clean, clinical, lacks warmth and character

recommendations.notes: Low shelf for broad warmth. Don't overdo - check for mud.
recommendations.context: Use on buses for overall warmth increase

recommendations.notes: More focused warmth boost
recommendations.context: For individual tracks needing warmth

rules.description: Mix lacks dimension, depth, or frequency spread - sounds flat

recommendations.notes: Detail adds dimension and perceived depth
recommendations.context: Start with detail in upper-mids

recommendations.notes: Air opens up the top and adds space
recommendations.context: Then add air for complete dimension

rules.description: Specific frequency that rings out or resonates unnaturally

recommendations.notes: Use notch filter for surgical removal. Sweep to find exact frequency.
recommendations.context: For obvious room modes or resonances - adjust frequency as needed

recommendations.notes: If resonance is in honk range (700-1000 Hz)
recommendations.context: Common in brass, guitars, vocals

recommendations.notes: If resonance is in upper-mid range (4-6 kHz)
recommendations.context: Sweep to find exact harsh resonance

rules.description: Vocals and bass are masking each other in the low-end

recommendations.notes: HP the vocals to separate from bass. This is essential.
recommendations.context: Apply to vocals - frees low-end for bass/kick

recommendations.notes: Also cut low-mids on vocals if still masking
recommendations.context: Further separation in warmth range

rules.description: Drums sound mushy, lack separation, or don't cut through

recommendations.notes: Remove boxiness from drum shells
recommendations.context: Common in snares, toms, room mics

recommendations.notes: Add attack and snap to drums
recommendations.context: Enhances stick definition and transients

contextualNotes.trackLevel: Use full gain ranges (up to ±6 dB), be more aggressive with EQ
contextualNotes.busLevel: Be gentler (max ±3 dB), changes affect multiple tracks
contextualNotes.masterLevel: Very subtle only (max ±1.5 dB), mostly for final polish
workflow: 1. Fix critical issues first (priority 1): rumble, mud, harshness
2. Address important issues (priority 2): boxiness, nasal, clarity, thin/thick
3. Apply final polish (priority 3): air, detail, dimension
